evidence.note: The menu presents genuine variety (Grapple control 71%, Set up position, two Safe offense options, Reset), so the decision space itself is fine; climb was chosen with no downside.
One big spot decides the match: 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick — Hall takes 19 damage' plus a bleed and a rattled tag, taking momentum to [5,0] on the player's second action.
Hall never gets a meaningful turn — 'Hall tries to rise but can't find it — still down and vulnerable to a cover!' is his second and last action, and he lands zero damage all match.

Finish arrives with the opponent at 113/132 HP (86% health) after only three player actions: 'Hitman hooks in sharpshooter! … Hall taps out!'; there is no arc, no comeback window and near_fall_count=0.
Pacing gate failed at 5 turns against the [8, 40] band, and position_diversity is only 3 — the match ends before any tactical texture develops.

Every option is labeled with intent, hit chance and a plain-language note, e.g. 'Set up position / Climb to the top rope (auto) — changes ring position to unlock a stronger follow-up'; single_choice_turns=0.
Top-rope menu is honest about risk — both dives labeled 'Big swing … top-rope payoff: high risk, huge crowd pop' with 'Climb down carefully' offered as the bail-out.
Pin is visible when legal: 'Cover — pinfall attempt (pin)' shown next to 'Sharpshooter (82%)' while Hall is GROUNDED (curation_pin_visible=true), so curation hides nothing important here.

Submission percentage is misleading in effect: the 82% is the chance to APPLY the hold, but the hold applies and wins in the same beat, so a new player would reasonably read '82%' as an 82% chance to win the match.

State-change copy is clear and distinct: 'Hall is busted open; blood streams down their face' and 'Hall is rattled — when they're forced up, big payoffs may open' explain the bleed and pending-groggy setup without jargon.

Almost nothing was exercised: five choices offered, three taken all match, and the collar-and-elbow / loop-tax systems this build is testing never came into play (no stale-tie-up lines anywhere in the transcript).
The bleed line 'The crowd gasps — Hall is busted open; blood streams down their face' is the one hook that invites another run to see what blood actually does mechanically.
Pin versus sharpshooter was a live fork at 113 HP and only the submission was tried, so the pin branch and any kickout drama remain unseen.

stickiness.rematch_reason: Five turns is too little to form an opinion about the match — the finish landed before any exchange developed — but the blood callout and the untested pin branch leave mild curiosity.
stickiness.next_experiment: Rerun seed 201 taking the cover at T5 instead of the sharpshooter, and choose Collar-and-elbow tie-up at T1 rather than climbing, to see whether the match reaches the 8-40 turn band and whether the loop-tax feedback appears at all.

evidence.note: Strongest beat in the match stacks three feedback layers: 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick — Hall takes 19 damage. / The crowd gasps — Hall is busted open; blood streams down their face. / Hall is rattled — when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.'
The rattled promise is never paid off — Hall fails his get-up on T4 and the match ends on T5, so the setup text writes a cheque the match never cashes.

Submission sequence is well staged in isolation (finish_sequence delays 1.0/1.5/0.0, 'Hall reaches for daylight… / The hold is cinched in deeper! / Hall taps out!') but resolves on the first attempt against an 86%-health opponent.
No drama metrics at all: near_fall_count=0, position_diversity=3, no reversal or kickout lines in the whole transcript; log_uniqueness_ratio 1.0 is trivially high because only 5 turns were logged.

top_issues.summary: Match ends on turn 5, below the [8, 40] pacing band, with the loser at 113/132 HP and zero damage dealt; an 82% submission taken at near-full opponent health ends the match instantly, which makes the finish feel like a shortcut rather than a payoff.
top_issues.suggested_area: Submission win gating by target health/momentum, or a mandatory escape/near-fall beat on early attempts

top_issues.summary: The blood and 'rattled' setup on T3 promise escalation, but the match ends two turns later with near_fall_count=0 and no reversal or kickout anywhere, so the abrupt sub-band finish reads as anticlimax rather than dominance.
top_issues.suggested_area: Finish pacing / near-fall requirement before a match-ending hold

top_issues.summary: The sharpshooter's '82%' is the chance to apply the hold, but applying it won the match in the same beat, actively teaching the wrong mental model to a novice.
top_issues.suggested_area: Submission label wording — distinguish apply chance from win chance in the curated note

top_issues.summary: This seed exercises none of the anti-loop feedback under test — no tie-up was ever used, so no 'stalls out' / 'predictable' / 'telegraphed' lines appear in the transcript.
top_issues.suggested_area: Playtest coverage — novice policy seeds that reach the grapple game
